newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates slip as German rate worries fade.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates slip as German rate worries fade.

text.p: Dutch money rates showed a tendency to slip on Tuesday as market nerves settled on fading worries of rising U.S. and German interest rates.
Dealers said they no longer expected an imminent rate rise in Germany as the dollar was trading well off its recent peak and German M3 growth for July slowed to 5.7 percent from 6.4 percent in June.
Analysts had forecast M3 growth of 6.3 percent for July.
Markets also do not expect a move from the U.S. Federal Reserve, which meets later today, or the German Bundesbank on Thursday.
"The euphoria is back in the market," said one dealer.
He added guilder rates could slip a bit further in the coming days. Six-month and one-year deposits were two basis points lower, bidding at respectively 3.48 and 3.66 percent.
One to three-month deposits were unchanged and call money rates were trading fractionally lower at 3.25 percent bid.
"Call money could also slip further as it does not look like there's a real shortage of liquidity ahead of the expiry of the current four-week cash reserve arrangement.
"It is very well possible that call money rates will drop below the 3.00 percent level," said one dealer.

On Monday one or more market players needed to acquire up to 25 million guilders at the marginal advances rate of 4.5 percent because their cash reserve account showed a debit balance at the end of the day.
"You can never be sure beforehand, but it looks like some participants have ample liquidity," said another dealer, adding he also foresaw a further drop in call money rates on Wednesday and Thursday.
The guilder was a touch weaker compared to the German mark at 112.6325 per 100 marks versus 112.61 on Monday.
The dollar was trading at 2.0642/47 guilders.
